draft.title: Expanded notation with powers of 10
card: Each digit in a number has a place value. Moving one place left makes the value 10 times bigger. The places are 1, 10, 100, 1000 and so on.
These place values are powers of 10: 1 = 10⁰, 10 = 10¹, 100 = 10², 1000 = 10³. The small raised number counts the tens multiplied together.
Expanded notation writes each digit times its power of 10, then adds them. A digit of 0 adds nothing, so that place can be left out.
4305 = 4 × 10³ + 3 × 10² + 5 × 10⁰. There are no tens, so there is no 10¹ term.
draft.remember: Write each digit times its place value as a power of 10, and add.

a.q: Which is 6208 in expanded notation using powers of 10?
a.why: The 6 is in the thousands place (10³), the 2 is in the hundreds (10²) and the 8 is in the ones (10⁰). Using 10¹ for the 8 is tempting, but 10¹ is the tens place and this number has 0 tens.
a.clue: Ones are 10⁰. Count the places moving left.

b.q: Mia writes a number as 7 × 10⁴ + 5 × 10² + 3 × 10⁰. What is the number?
b.why: 7 × 10⁴ is 70 000, 5 × 10² is 500 and 3 × 10⁰ is 3, so the total is 70 503. The answer 7503 is tempting, but it ignores that 10⁴ is ten thousands, and the missing 10³ and 10¹ terms mean zeros in those places.
b.clue: Find which places have no term. They hold zeros.

final.title: Expanded notation with powers of 10
card: Each digit in a number has a place value. Moving one place left makes the value 10 times bigger. The places are 1, 10, 100, 1000 and so on.
These place values are powers of 10: \(1 = 10^{0}\), \(10 = 10^{1}\), \(100 = 10^{2}\), \(1000 = 10^{3}\). The small raised number counts the tens multiplied together.
Expanded notation writes each digit times its power of 10, then adds them. A digit of 0 adds nothing, so that place can be left out.
\(4305 = 4 \times 10^{3} + 3 \times 10^{2} + 5 \times 10^{0}\). There are no tens, so there is no \(10^{1}\) term.
final.remember: Write each digit times its place value as a power of 10, and add.

a.q: Which is 6208 in expanded notation using powers of 10?
a.why: The 6 is in the thousands place \((10^{3})\), the 2 is in the hundreds \((10^{2})\) and the 8 is in the ones \((10^{0})\). Using \(10^{1}\) for the 8 is tempting, but \(10^{1}\) is the tens place and this number has 0 tens.
a.clue: Ones are \(10^{0}\). Count the places moving left.

b.q: Mia writes a number as \(7 \times 10^{4} + 5 \times 10^{2} + 3 \times 10^{0}\). What is the number?
b.why: \(7 \times 10^{4}\) is 70 000, \(5 \times 10^{2}\) is 500 and \(3 \times 10^{0}\) is 3, so the total is 70 503. The answer 7503 is tempting, but it ignores that \(10^{4}\) is ten thousands, and the missing \(10^{3}\) and \(10^{1}\) terms mean zeros in those places.
b.clue: Find which places have no term. They hold zeros.
